spiritual_reading.full_translation:
A full set of complete discernments stands in being: mighty Divine faculties of righteous decision. They go forth from the highest Divine degree and enter the created domain, and each is appointed to its own use according to the will of the one Divine Discerner. This Discerner is above every particular discernment, established in eternal Divine states; it is the hidden, immeasurable Divine Source.

The first discernment is the primal good that first met ruling falsity at the beginning and brought it low. It pronounced righteous decision against that arrogance, because it had lifted itself up against a dominion that was not its own.

The second discernment is living Divine operation proceeding, which came to sustain what had been assaulted. It rendered judgement upon the whole host of evils that had torn and violated the outer forms by which the primal good could act and appear.

The third discernment is the wisdom-principle proceeding from love, which arranged the higher spiritual degree into beauty and order according to the Divine delight entrusted to it. It judged the dominant evils in the higher region, restraining them and fixing them firmly in the state that fits what they had made themselves.

The fourth discernment is the formative Divine operation that establishes a new state of blessedness. It made righteous judgement upon the hidden interiors of the adversary, so that spiritual death might no longer surge up from that time on. It set a fixed restraint upon evil; and at the summit of this new formation it established a governing union for the primal good and for all who are in the origin of heavenly truth—those who engaged in spiritual combat with evil and overcame it.

The fifth discernment is the Divine rule of honor abiding in full completion in the highest outward degree. It discerns all outward degrees, giving true and righteous decision upon every power and every dominion that operates in external appearances.

The sixth discernment is the proceeding Divine presence that mediates between the highest and the lower. It made the Divine likeness manifest, and purified the good of wisdom that had been mixed and obscured, separating what is genuinely Divine from what had been seized and defiled by the adversary; here the mode of completion is broken in the record, but the action continues as a work of separation and restoration.

The seventh discernment governs the ordering of the domains of life by the laws of spiritual combat. It grants victory to those who remain firm in good and truth, and condemns those proven to be in confirmed evil and falsity. For the steadfast it becomes the ordered progression of advance in their uses; but the convicted it drives away and consigns to the lowest state, far from heavenly influx.

The eighth discernment is the Divine enlightening presence that leads those who proclaim truth. After the Divine likeness had been made manifest and the purified good of wisdom had been received, evils and falsities rose up from interior and exterior levels in resistance; therefore this enlightening presence went forth, entered the outward degrees, and executed judgement there, separating those constant in good from those convicted of evil.

The ninth discernment is the purity of heavenly truth in receptive form, which by manifested holiness draws the inmost affections even of opposed powers and gathers what is its own into unity. It judges the dominion of persuasive, flowing falsity and the dominion of hardened, resisting falsity.

The tenth discernment is Divine scrutiny in the intermediate region between inner and outer life, judging the human race in general states. It separates those who are in good from those who are in evil, setting the just apart from those who live in sin.

The eleventh discernment is enlightened understanding from heaven that will be manifested within the human condition. It chooses the holy community that lives from love and truth, unveils what has been hidden, separates wisdom from falsity, and sets genuine truth apart from lawlessness.

The twelfth discernment is the great ordering counsel: the call to use and the obedience of reception, appointed in the most external fundamentals of life. It performs the final separation between the good and the evil; and at the end it gathers the whole into a last, complete form, bringing all things into a final fixed order, and again separates wisdom from falsity.

These are the complete discernments sent forth. They proceed from the one Divine Discerner above them all: the hidden and immeasurable Divine Source, established in eternal Divine states in supreme governing order and honor, reigning by Divine love within Divine wisdom.

paragraph_translations.translation: A full set of complete discernments stands in being: mighty Divine faculties of righteous decision. They go forth from the highest Divine degree and enter the created domain, and each is appointed to its own use according to the will of the one Divine Discerner who entrusts each discerning to its proper function. This Discerner is above every particular discernment, established in eternal Divine states; it is the hidden Divine Source of greatness itself.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the chapter’s frame by stating the origin, descent, and ordering of all discernments under one supreme Discerner.

paragraph_translations.translation: The first discernment is the primal good that first met ruling falsity at the beginning and brought it low. It pronounced righteous decision against that arrogance, because it had lifted itself up against a dominion that was not its own.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by naming the first discernment and its initial judgement against arrogating evil.

paragraph_translations.translation: The second discernment is living Divine operation proceeding, which came to sustain what had been assaulted. It rendered judgement upon the whole host of evils that had torn and violated the outer forms by which the primal good could act and appear.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by moving from the first combat to restorative judgement on the violating powers.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Outer forms” is forced by the damaged-clothing image; the exact nuance (truths, appearances, or powers of action) is compressed.

paragraph_translations.translation: The third discernment is the wisdom-principle proceeding from love, which arranged the higher spiritual degree into beauty and order according to the Divine delight entrusted to it. It judged the dominant evils in the higher region, restraining them and fixing them firmly in the state that fits what they had made themselves.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the ordering function: wisdom beautifies higher order and restrains dominant evils.

paragraph_translations.translation: The fourth discernment is the formative Divine operation that establishes a new state of blessedness. It made righteous judgement upon the hidden interiors of the adversary, so that spiritual death might no longer surge up from that time on. It set a fixed restraint upon evil; and at the summit of this new formation it established a governing union for the primal good and for all who are in the origin of heavenly truth—those who engaged in spiritual combat with evil and overcame it.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by describing deep restraint of evil and establishment of a supreme governing order for the victors.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Hidden interiors” is the closest spiritual rendering for the storehouse image; “governing union” condenses crown/throne into one governing highest principle.

paragraph_translations.translation: The fifth discernment is the Divine rule of honor abiding in full completion in the highest outward degree. It discerns all outward degrees, giving true and righteous decision upon every power and every dominion that operates in external appearances.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES the list by shifting to judgement over outward degrees and their regimes.
paragraph_translations.notes: The “full completion” reading leans on the sevenfold/firmament phrasing; exact cosmology is secondary to degree-language.

paragraph_translations.translation: The sixth discernment is the proceeding Divine presence that mediates between the highest and the lower. It made the Divine likeness manifest, and purified the good of wisdom that had been mixed and obscured, separating what is genuinely Divine from what had been seized and defiled by the adversary.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by moving from ruling judgement to mediating manifestation and purification.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source line is fragmentary at the end; the completion is inferred as continued separation/cleansing.

paragraph_translations.translation: The seventh discernment governs the ordering of the domains of life by the laws of spiritual combat. It grants victory to those who remain firm in good and truth, and condemns those proven to be in confirmed evil and falsity. For the steadfast it becomes the ordered progression of advance in their uses; but the convicted it drives away and consigns to the lowest state, far from heavenly influx.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the theme of separation by describing outcomes for steadfast versus convicted states.
paragraph_translations.notes: This paragraph is heavily broken; “domains of life” and “ordered progression” are best-fit reconstructions, and the ‘steps of the way’ phrase remains uncertain.

paragraph_translations.translation: The eighth discernment is the Divine enlightening presence that leads those who proclaim truth. After the Divine likeness had been made manifest and the purified good of wisdom had been received, evils and falsities rose up from interior and exterior levels in resistance; therefore this enlightening presence went forth, entered the outward degrees, and executed judgement there, separating those constant in good from those convicted of evil.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES the conflict-response cycle: resistance arises and a descending enlightenment judges.
paragraph_translations.notes: Named figure functions as an enlightening, apostolic-leading presence; details between ‘came…descended’ are broken in the source but the action is clear.

paragraph_translations.translation: The ninth discernment is the purity of heavenly truth in receptive form, which by manifested holiness draws the inmost affections even of opposed powers and gathers what is its own into unity. It judges the dominion of persuasive, flowing falsity and the dominion of hardened, resisting falsity.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by shifting from public judgement to interior attraction and discrimination between two falsity-regimes.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Moist” and “dry” are rendered as two opposite modes of falsity; the precise moral psychology may vary with the tradition’s internal usage.

paragraph_translations.translation: The tenth discernment is Divine scrutiny in the intermediate region between inner and outer life, judging the human race in general states. It separates those who are in good from those who are in evil, setting the just apart from those who live in sin.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by applying judgement universally in a middle degree of life.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Intermediate region” is the spiritual replacement for the atmospheric image.

paragraph_translations.translation: The eleventh discernment is enlightened understanding from heaven that will be manifested within the human condition. It chooses the holy community that lives from love and truth, unveils what has been hidden, separates wisdom from falsity, and sets genuine truth apart from lawlessness.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by turning to revelation within human life and the gathering of a holy community.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Holy community” condenses the ecclesial image without preserving natural-language institutions.

paragraph_translations.translation: The twelfth discernment is the great ordering counsel: the call to use and the obedience of reception, appointed in the most external fundamentals of life. It performs the final separation between the good and the evil; and at the end it gathers the whole into a last, complete form, bringing all things into a final fixed order, and again separates wisdom from falsity.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS into the final, ultimate ordering and last-form consolidation.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Most external fundamentals” replaces elemental language; “last, complete form” replaces the statue image while preserving the idea of ultimate fixed embodiment.

paragraph_translations.translation: These are the complete and mighty discernments that go forth. They proceed from the one Divine Discerner above them all: the hidden and immeasurable Divine Source that is, established in eternal Divine states in supreme governing order and honor, reigning within its own kingdom of Divine greatness.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES and closes by returning all discernments to their single transcendent origin.
paragraph_translations.notes: The closing piles titles; they are unified into a single description of the supreme Divine Source without retaining courtly objects.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Strongly coherent as a single ordered doctrine of successive Divine discernments operating through degrees, culminating in final separation and ultimate form. Coherence weakens only where the source is physically fragmentary (paragraphs 8–10, especially 9), forcing reconstructed transitions and generalized phrasing.

findings.diagnosis: Clean chapter frame: a numbered set of judges dispatched from a transcendent Judge; no narrative break. The teaching mode is primarily administrative (hierarchy/commission) but functions as the chapter’s heading and stays consistent with the ensuing list.
findings.evidence: Text: “Twelve judges exist… They were sent… assigned to different works according to the command… the great Judge… is the Father of Greatness.” The spiritual reading did not stumble here; it treated it as an organizing frame (“origin, descent, and ordering… under one supreme Discerner”), which matches the commission/jurisdiction diction in the Coptic (sent/assigned/command).

findings.diagnosis: Clean list-items where administrative titles are integrated into an action-description (judging/constructing/fettering). This reads like a stable catalogue tradition, not a later seam-expansion. The spiritual reading remains smooth because each named figure participates as an acting judge, not merely a name in a roster.
findings.evidence: Text is title + functional act: “First Man… judged…”, “Living Spirit… bore up… made a judgement…”, “Mother of Life… beautified and set up… fettered…”, “Great Builder… built… judged… constructed a prison… constructed a throne…”, “King of Honour… is the judge… gives a true judgement… upon all the powers and all the kingdoms.” Stage-3a reading stays coherent here; its only strain is interpretive (e.g., “storehouses”→“hidden interiors”), not narrative disruption.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from physical damage/fragmentation, not an insertion. The spiritual reading had to generalize and reconstruct transitions because the exemplar is broken, especially at the end of ¶8 and throughout ¶9 and parts of ¶10.
findings.evidence: Text signals lacunae: ¶8 ends “he has [separated it]”; ¶9 is mostly ellipses and uncertain phrase “steps of the way (?)”; ¶10 has multiple breaks “He came ... ... he descended”. The reading explicitly flags this: “mode of completion is broken in the record” (¶8), “heavily broken… best-fit reconstructions… uncertain” (¶9), “details… are broken… but the action is clear” (¶10). Removing any of this would not improve coherence; the list requires items 6–8 and the breaks are manuscript-level.

findings.diagnosis: Possible minor christological/institutional overlay in the appositive ‘father of all the apostles’, but it does not break the chapter’s list-logic and may be integral to this chapter’s Manichaean judge-catalogue. If secondary, it is a small gloss rather than a block insertion.
findings.evidence: Text: “The eighth judge is Jesus the Splendour, the father of all the apostles”. The spiritual reading notes it functionally (“apostolic-leading presence”) and continues without stumbling; that suggests it is not a disruptive seam. Still, “father of all the apostles” is exactly the kind of ecclesial-title add-on that can attach to a named hypostasis without contributing to the judging action (which comes after: “made a judgement… separated…”).
findings.scope: Annotate the appositive gloss-like title in ¶10: “the father of all the apostles” as potentially ecclesial/identificatory overlay attached to the judge-name.

findings.diagnosis: Clean continuation: each judge is identified and given a judging/separating function. The reading’s only pressure points are interpretive (moist/dry; atmosphere), not textual incoherence.
findings.evidence: Text is consistent: ¶11 “Virgin of Light… makes a judgement on the ruler of the moist, and the ruler of the dry”; ¶12 “Judge who dwells in the atmosphere… makes a separation…”; ¶13 “Light Mind… chooses the holy church… unveils… separates…” The spiritual reading acknowledges substitution choices (“rendered as two opposite modes”; “intermediate region”; “holy community”), but it does not report narrative breaks or non-participating names.

findings.diagnosis: Administrative/institutional mechanism intrudes into the judge-list: the ‘great counsel’ is immediately equated with a bureaucratic-sounding pair (“summons and the obedience”) and is “appointed in the elements.” This is less a personified judge doing an act and more a system of governance. The spiritual reading smooths it by abstracting heavily (“call to use… obedience of reception… most external fundamentals”), which is a sign it had to translate institutional language back into correspondential process.
findings.evidence: Text: “The twelfth judge is the great counsel, which is the summons and the obedience… appointed in the elements… sculpt its own self in the Last Statue.” This is classic mechanism-language (summons/obedience/appointment) rather than a hypostasis acting like the prior judges. The reading’s need to replace terms (“most external fundamentals” for “elements”; “last, complete form” for “Last Statue”) indicates conceptual mismatch with its functional narrative style, even though it can be made to cohere.
findings.scope: Annotate ¶14 as an administrative/institutional overlay formulation within the list (especially the equivalence ‘great counsel = summons and obedience’ and ‘appointed in the elements’). Do not excise, because it is presented as the twelfth item rather than a detachable inserted block.

findings.diagnosis: Clean inclusio/closure returning to the transcendent source; no seam. The piling of titles is stylistically administrative but is exactly what a catalogue colophon looks like and matches ¶2’s frame.
findings.evidence: Text: “These are the twelve… They came from the great Judge… Father that is hidden and immeasurable… throne of honour… King of Honour…” The spiritual reading reports no stumble and treats it as closure; narratively it completes the frame begun in ¶2.

textual_criticism.summary: 7 findings: 4 clean confirmations (¶2; ¶3-¶7; ¶11-¶13; ¶15), 1 genuine-damage difficulty (¶8-¶10), and 2 likely overlay notes recommended for annotation (a small ecclesial gloss in ¶10; an institutional/mechanism formulation in ¶14). No excisions recommended, because the major coherence pressures arise from manuscript lacunae rather than detachable administrative insertions, and the administrative elements that stand out are embedded as list-items rather than separable blocks.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Twelve judges exist; the great mighty givers of judgement! They were sent and came from the exalted greatness to this place. They were assigned to different works according to the command that the Judge, who belongs to the greatness, entrusted to all these judges. Now he, the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges, who exists and is established in the aeons of greatness; he is the Father of Greatness.

The first judge is the First Man, he who humiliated the ruler of Darkness in the beginning. He judged him according to a judgement of righteousness; for he had exalted himself against a kingdom that was not his own.
The second judge is the Living Spirit, he who came and bore up the Man. He too made a judgement on all the powers of darkness; which had wounded the garments of the First Man.

The third judge is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, she who beautified and set up the heavenly part of the universe, according to her pleasure; which [was entrusted to] her. She judged the rulers above; she fettered and set them firmly in the place that is fitting for them.

The fourth judge is the Great Builder, he who built the new aeon of joy. He judged, according to a judgement of righteousness, the storehouses of the enemy; that death may not well up from this time on. He has constructed a prison for the enemy. Also, upon the crown of the building he has constructed a throne for the First Man and all the fathers of light; they who engaged the struggle with the evil one and were victorious over him.

⟨p.80⟩
The fifth judge is the great King of Honour, he who dwells and is established in the seventh firmament. He is the judge of all the firmaments who gives a true judgement, according to a judgement of righteousness, upon all the powers and all the kingdoms of the firmaments.
The sixth judge is [the Th]ird Ambassador, he who came and displayed his image. He purified the light [that was mingled] which his own [image had seized] also of the enemy, he has [separated it]

The seventh judge is ... ... the worlds [as he gives the victory to] they who are steadfast; but he condemns the ones who are convicted ... ... he shall become for them the steps of the way (?) [in their works; for the steadfast]; but the convicted he sweeps and casts out to the depths.

The eighth judge is Jesus the Splendour, the father of all the apostles; because after the Ambassador had displayed his image and the light was taken [up;] a mass of rulers rose up from above and below. Then they sent Jesus the Splendour. He came ... ... he descended and made a judgement in the firmaments. He separated the steadfast from the convicted.

The ninth judge is the Virgin of Light, [she who took the heart] of the powers by her image, gathering her own ones into her. She makes a judgement on the ruler of the moist, and the ruler of the dry.
The tenth judge is the Judge who dwells in the atmosphere, judging all mankind. He makes a separation between they who are good and they who are evil, setting apart the righteous from the sinners.

⟨p.81⟩
The eleventh judge is the Light Mind, he who shall come and appear in the world. And he chooses the holy church, and he unveils [the hidden things] and separates light from darkness, and sets the truth apart from lawlessness.

The twelfth judge is the great counsel, which is the summons and the obedience, which is appointed in the elements. It is the one that makes a separation between the good and the evil ones. At the end also it can gather itself together and sculpt its own self in the Last Statue. And it separates light from darkness.

These are the twelve great and mighty judges who were sent. They came from the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges. He is the Father that is hidden and immeasurable, the one who exists; who is established in the aeons of greatness upon the great throne of honour, which is the King of Honour [who reigns] in his kingdom.

changes_summary: No changes made. The critic issued no excise recommendations (Findings 1–3, 5, 7 = none; Findings 4 and 6 = annotate only, which requires no modification to the chapter text).
